messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after landing the INT8 TP patch (reduce-scales + dynamic-kernel-select) we see a 25-40% tail-latency regression on multi-GPU long-context workloads. Attached a short perf sketch below.
ajay: Ugh, that’s big. Is it across all sequence lengths or just long ones? :thinking_face:
derek: Looks like long contexts (>=8k tokens) primarily, but microbatching for throughput also increased p99 on shorter seqs.
sophia: I pulled a perf trace from staging. Major time spent in NCCL allreduce and in a fallback matmul kernel.
maria: Paste from flamegraph (abbreviated):
```
GPU compute (kernels fused)        40ms
NCCL allreduce                     85ms
kernel selector fallback: gemm_fp32 60ms
KV cache shard sync (serial)       30ms
Other CPU scheduling               20ms
Total step                         235ms
```
maria: The kernel selector seems to prefer an optimized INT8 fused-gemm for most layers but falls back to a slow path for narrow-dim matmuls produced by the TP sharding pattern.
liam: Do we see increased KV cache invalidations or migrations with the new batching heuristics? That could serialize comms.
maria: Yes — KV sharding combined with the aggressive packer causes frequent small allreduces for cache-coherence. Those small allreduces are not being batched on the NCCL level, so latency dominates.
derek: Two hypotheses: 1) kernel fallback for small M/K dims is much slower in fp32 fallback, 2) NCCL streams/algorithms choose non-opt trees for many small messages causing high startup cost.
sophia: I repro'd locally — when I force the kernel selector to prefer fused_int8 for the narrow dims, compute time drops ~30ms but NCCL cost stays high.
infra-bot: gpu-ci-bot run:perf-trace 1934567890 --target=multi-gpu-longctx --quant=int8
ajay: Possible mitigations: increase KV aggregation window, merge small allreduces into a single batched reduce, or alter packer to avoid creating tiny microbatches that cross TP boundaries.
maria: Also the FP8/INT8 scaling looks noisy per-layer under TP: some layers produce scale underflow and trigger dequant->requant paths, which fall back to safe kernels.
liam: Can we try two quick experiments?
- disable the packer crossing TP shards (cheap config toggle)
- force NCCL algorithm to ring / tree to compare startup vs bandwidth
maria: Commands I used to repro (staging):
```bash
export REDWOOD_QUANT_MODE=int8
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECT=dynamic
export NCCL_ALGO=auto
python serve_multi_gpu.py --model redwood-v2-13b --tp 8 --seq-len 8192 --microbatch 2 --kv-shard true
```
maria: To force different NCCL algo set NCCL_ALGO=ring or NCCL_ALGO=tree and restart the runtime.
derek: I'll run the packer toggle locally and post traces. If packing is creating cross-shard fragments, fixing the packer might eliminate a ton of small allreduces.
sophia: I can try an INT8 scaling calibration pass that stores per-layer scales at load time (avoid runtime recalibration). That should reduce the fallback triggers.
liam: We should also add a kernel selector rule: when TP causes very small K dims, prefer the fused path or a specialized narrow-gemm kernel — cheaper than falling back to full fp32 matmul.
ajay: Agreed. Short-term plan:
- derek: validate packer-cross-tp toggle and share perf trace (ETA 4h)
- sophia: run scale-calibration and report kernel-fallback counts (ETA 6h)
- liam: prototype a selector hint for narrow dims and benchmark (ETA EOD)
- maria: coordinate staging test runs and collate traces
If any of these reduces the number of NCCL small-reduces we should see p99 drop a lot.
maria: FYI I also saw some scheduling jitter on the host that serialized GPU launches. Adding a dedicated NCCL stream per TP shard improved overlap in a quick test.
infra-bot: Note: inc. 1934567890 assigned to eng-runtime "tp-int8-kv-comm" (auto-created)
gpu-ci-bot: Perf run queued (job 45233). Will upload traces here when done.
liam: One more ask — can we log per-layer kernel choice and quant state (fast-path vs fallback) in the perf traces? That will make root-cause clear.
maria: Good call, liam. I'll add a lightweight counter to the runtime and include it in the next trace.
ajay: Thanks team. If anyone finds a quick config fix that buys headroom for the weekend, ping infra to roll a patch to staging. :rocket:
maria: I'll post initial traces in this thread as soon as gpu-ci-bot finishes. Thanks all.
